video.title: ModelContainer, Query & ModelContext | Day 176
video.description:
Learn to explain how SwiftData saves and loads models in a SwiftUI app: ModelContainer, Query & ModelContext, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
ModelContainer - An object that sets up where your SwiftData models are stored.
Query - A property wrapper that fetches saved models and keeps the view up to date.
ModelContext - The workspace where you insert, change and delete SwiftData models.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

dialogue.title: Saving notes

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I want my notes to stay after the app closes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use SwiftData. First, create a ModelContainer for the app.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It sets up where the models are stored on the device.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay. How do I show the saved notes in a list?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use Query. It loads the models and updates the view when they change.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I write `@Query var notes`, and no fetch code?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right, the Query does the fetching for you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And how do I save a new note?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Read the ModelContext from the environment, then call `insert`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I called save by hand, but it did nothing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Check the ModelContext. It usually saves on its own, so make sure the ModelContainer is set.
Create one ModelContainer for the whole app.
